definitions.name: NATS Connection Check
definitions.documentation: Connection Check. Native official NATS transport-node3.4.0 embedded with Apache-2.0 and transitive notices. Fresh bounded TCP/TLS connection, no reconnect or replay. TLS requires handshake-first server with CA/hostname verification; explicit disable is plaintext. RuntimeConnection nested config/credentials via builtin $connection; numeric retries=0 or absent on raw node/profile before secrets. Mutations require confirm=true. Total deadline includes profile/secrets/driver/wire and is shortened by profile. Payload64KiB, wire1MiB, headers8KiB/64, messages100, frames2048; APIs return one bounded page and reject unsafe integer precision. Published means flushed to server, never processed. No persistent triggers, subscriptions, JWT/nkey files, HTTP bridge or app dependency installer. Synthetic protocol proof only; no real provider validation. Sources: https://docs.nats.io/ https://github.com/nats-io/nats.js/tree/v3.4.0 https://docs.nats.io/reference/reference-protocols/nats-protocol https://docs.nats.io/reference/reference-protocols/nats_api_reference

definitions.description: Typed event emitted by NATS Message Received (Relay).
definitions.documentation: Event output contract for NATS Message Received (Relay). This trigger accepts the canonical version-1 nats envelope only; it does not authenticate or decode native provider requests. Required exact provider verification: Deploy an independently managed TLS/authenticated NATS subscriber/JetStream consumer with restricted subjects, explicit durable consumer, bounded inflight limits and authorized stream/account. Do not expose a raw NATS listener on ONF. Mapping: Emit message.received with exact subject, byte payload base64, stream and decimal stream sequence when JetStream is used. Core NATS uses null stream/sequence and a durable relay-assigned ID; JetStream deliveryId uses stream plus sequence. Canonical eventType values: message.received. Required envelope: version=1, provider=nats, deliveryId, eventType, occurredAt (UTC ISO milliseconds), accountId, resource as the typed output schema. Omit no required fields; use explicit null where allowed. Filters accountId/resourceId are exact matches; blank disables a filter. At most 100 account+delivery IDs within 96 KiB deduplicate retries per group; state commits on trigger success before downstream completion. Relay owns ack/NAK/Term/progress/replay policy; no acknowledgement is issued by ONF. Core NATS is transient; JetStream acknowledgement does not imply downstream workflow success. Sources: https://docs.nats.io/learn/jetstream/pull-consumers https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream/consumers

ingressRequirements.name: NATS and JetStream messages relay
ingressRequirements.description: Manual prerequisite: separately maintained exact provider authentication/normalization relay. This release only accepts header-authenticated canonical envelopes from that relay.
setupSteps: Install this reviewed package release; no relay or subscription is installed.
Deploy an independently maintained provider-aware relay which implements the exact provider signature, challenge, authorization and replay rules described below.

Deploy an independently managed TLS/authenticated NATS subscriber/JetStream consumer with restricted subjects, explicit durable consumer, bounded inflight limits and authorized stream/account. Do not expose a raw NATS listener on ONF.

Emit message.received with exact subject, byte payload base64, stream and decimal stream sequence when JetStream is used. Core NATS uses null stream/sequence and a durable relay-assigned ID; JetStream deliveryId uses stream plus sequence.

Implement the exact canonical version-1 envelope and typed resource schemas documented by each selected trigger; forward one event per POST. Normalize account identity from the authorized provider connection, never from an untrusted request.

Persist one stable delivery ID per logical event across relay retries. Fanout IDs must include distinct native entity/event/status identity (or a persisted record ID); reusing a batch delivery ID or message ID across different statuses drops events. Authorize account/resources; bound payloads to 64 KiB and limit rate.
Save a separate relay-to-ONF callback secret; create a header-authenticated ingress profile for this requirement.
Bind the intended trigger node, configure the relay with its HTTPS callback URL, then deliberately enable workflow and entry.
Review relay limits, delivery identifiers, retries and downstream idempotency; test explicitly before production use.

Select saved node entry mode webhook explicitly; package metadata does not infer it. Create/select a profile for this exact installed requirement (installation.id + "/verified-events"), bind node.trigger.ingress.profileId, save the graph and deliberately enable workflow and entry only when setup is complete.
